dedupe_keys.name: nlr agile autonomous grids identification learning and estimation tcp data bridge for streaming and replaying grid sensor data

description: AGILE is a National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) software platform that helps grid operators and researchers sort through and aggregate large volumes of power system sensor data. Contents: a data bridge that connects data repositories, data sharing and analysis tools over a standard Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) interface instead of tool-specific APIs; it aggregates data from multiple repositories without changing MATLAB or Python configurations, lets data stored in InfluxDB and Kafka be streamed or subscribed to by any application that can open a TCP connection, and can replay data from chosen time windows as if reported in real time. It is built on JavaScript and Node.js and deployed in containers, and feeds analyses such as system identification, nonlinear dynamics, stability assessment and machine learning. Producer: NLR grid modernization research (contact Struan Clark, Computational Science Center). Coverage: generic sensor data (for example high-resolution grid measurements). Format and access: the page gives no download or repository link; contact the developer. Licence: not stated on the NLR page. Caveats: availability outside NLR is not stated; the page was last updated in March 2026. Simulation uses: feeding measured or replayed grid sensor streams into state estimation, stability analysis and digital twin experiments.
